name: Deuterium Formation
description: A proton and neutron bind together via the strong force to form deuterium

layman.title: Building a Heavier Hydrogen
layman.summary: Watch a proton and neutron snap together to form the nucleus of heavy hydrogen

sections.whatsHappening: A neutron is approaching a proton. When they get close enough — within about 1 femtometer (a millionth of a billionth of a millimeter) — the strong nuclear force grabs them and pulls them together. They bind into a deuteron, the nucleus of deuterium (heavy hydrogen). A photon is released carrying away the excess binding energy.
sections.whyItMatters: This is the first step in nuclear fusion — the process that powers every star in the universe. Inside the Sun, protons and neutrons combine to build helium, releasing enormous amounts of energy. Deuterium formation is also being studied for fusion power reactors on Earth.
sections.whatToWatch: Watch the gray neutron approach the red proton from the right. When they get close, they snap together and a pulsing glow appears between them — that's the strong force binding. A yellow photon shoots away, carrying the 2.22 MeV of binding energy.
sections.funFact: About 1 in every 6,400 hydrogen atoms in ocean water is actually deuterium. That's enough that if we could fuse all the deuterium in a single gallon of seawater, it would produce as much energy as burning 300 gallons of gasoline!

scientific.narrative: A free neutron approaches a proton. At distances below ~2 fm, the strong nuclear force (mediated by pion exchange) overcomes the centrifugal barrier and binds the two nucleons into a deuteron — the only bound state of the two-nucleon system. The deuteron has spin-1 (triplet state), isospin-0, and a binding energy of 2.224 MeV. The excess energy is radiated as a gamma-ray photon. The deuteron is weakly bound compared to heavier nuclei, with no excited states.
